question: A 110,000 g crate sits on a factory conveyor. Its acceleration in m/s² is found by taking the number of ways to choose 3 items from a set of 6, adding 28, subtracting 19, and then subtracting 25. The conveyor belt is 22 m long. What force must the drive supply to give the crate this acceleration, in N?

A 75 kg sled on a test track is accelerated at a rate in m/s² found by taking 7 times the sum of 7 and 2, subtracting 20, and then subtracting 2. The booster must supply the thrust needed for this. The track is 450 m long. Five sleds run together, so the combined thrust is 5 times the single-sled value, and the combined thrust is converted to kN. What is the combined thrust, in kN?

A 127,000 g die on a press is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the smaller root of x² - 6x + 8 = 0. Twelve identical rams each supply the force needed for this, and the press sums the 12 outputs and converts the sum to kN. The press log records a net force by adding a 7 kN hydraulic assist and then subtracting a 23 kN return-spring load, with the pressing direction positive, so it may be negative. What net force does the log record, in kN?

A 99 kg crate on a warehouse conveyor is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the smaller root of x² - 5x + 4 = 0. The drive supplies the force needed for this, less 6 N contributed by a slight incline. The conveyor belt is 16 m long. Eleven conveyors run per floor, so the floor figure is 11 times the per-conveyor value, plus 5 N of margin. Three floors operate, so the site total is 3 times the floor figure. What is the site total, in N?

The figure the depot manager finally wants is twice the total kinetic energy of a whole rake of 12 identical ore carts, expressed in kilojoules, because the rake makes 2 loaded runs per shift. Each cart has a mass of 50000 g. On the downhill section every cart rolls at a speed, in metres per second, equal to 3 times the sum of 3 and 8. Work out the kinetic energy of a single cart in joules, then the total for all 12 carts, convert that total to kilojoules, and finally double it for the 2 runs. What is the resulting value in kJ?

A test engineer needs the combined push that a rig must supply to 11 identical sleds at once, in newtons. Each sled has a mass of 87000 g. The rig's controller sets the acceleration of a sled, in metres per second squared, from a calibration rule: take the instantaneous rate of change of the curve 3x^3 - 2x^2 with respect to x at the point x = 1, subtract 6 from it, then add 20. With the acceleration fixed, determine the push needed for one sled, and then the total for all 11 sleds moving together. What is that combined push in N?

In a foundry, a trolley of mass 55 kg is pulled along a 30 m rail by a winch cable. The trolley's acceleration in metres per second squared is the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. Find the pull needed to give the trolley that acceleration, in newtons, and convert it to kilonewtons. The cable also carries a steady 9 kN preload and a further 7 kN from a counterweight, both of which add to that figure, while a 5 kN reduction is applied for the winch's brake assist. What is the resulting cable tension in kN?

The number the crane inspector ultimately writes down is the load rating for the full set of 11 hoist lines, in kilonewtons. Each hoist line carries 10 identical lifting frames, and each frame has a mass of 42000 g and a hook width of 3 m. During the test lift, every frame accelerates upward at a rate, in metres per second squared, equal to the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 8 equals zero. Find the net push required on a single frame in newtons, convert it to kilonewtons, multiply by the 10 frames on one line, and add the line's own 9 kN safety allowance. The inspector's rating is that per-line figure multiplied by the 11 lines. What is the rating in kN?

A cargo elevator platform in a warehouse has a mass of 158000 g. Its upward acceleration in metres per second squared is set by adding 10 to the rate of change of the curve 4x^3 + 4x^2 with respect to x at x = 1. Find the push in newtons that produces this acceleration. A counterweight supplies 21 N of that push, so the hoist motor must provide the remainder. Express the motor's share in kilonewtons. What is the motor's share in kN?

The value the packaging engineer reports is the total kinetic energy, in kilojoules, of 3 batches of parcels, where each batch contains 4 identical parcels. Each parcel has a mass of 7 kg. On the conveyor every parcel moves at a speed, in metres per second, equal to the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0. Find the kinetic energy in joules of one parcel, multiply by 4 for a batch, multiply by 3 for all the batches, and convert the result to kilojoules. What is the total in kJ?

A maglev test bogie of mass 116000 g runs in a hall kept at 18 degrees Celsius. Its acceleration in metres per second squared equals the area under the curve 3x^2 + 2x between x = 0 and x = 2. Find the propulsive force in newtons needed to give the bogie that acceleration. The bogie is one of 6 identical bogies coupled into a train, so multiply the force by 6 to get the force for the whole train, and convert that to kilonewtons. The guideway adds 9 kN of magnetic braking drag that the propulsion must also overcome, so add 9 kN. What is the total propulsive force in kN?

What the range officer wants at the end of the session is a single energy figure in kilojoules: the total for 4 rounds of firing, each round consisting of 3 identical shots, plus an 11 kJ allowance for the energy stored in the launcher's spring. Each shot propels a 53 kg dummy payload along a 120 m range. The payload's speed in metres per second is the second derivative of 1x^3 + 2x^2 with respect to x evaluated at x = 2. Find the kinetic energy of one payload in joules and convert it to kilojoules; multiply by 3 for one round, then by 4 for all rounds, and finally add the 11 kJ allowance. What is the officer's figure in kJ?

The quantity the lab needs is the kinetic energy, in joules, of a 44 kg test dummy at the moment its sled is released. The sled's speed in metres per second is dialled in by the control software as follows: start with the greatest common divisor of 338 and 215, multiply it by 8, multiply the result by 9, subtract 30, and then add 10. The dummy sits on a sled running along a rail in a crash-test hall. Using the mass and the computed speed, determine the dummy's kinetic energy. What is that energy in J?

What the site foreman ultimately needs is the combined rating of 9 identical hydraulic rams, in kilonewtons. Each ram handles 8 identical pallets, and each pallet of mass 98 kg must be accelerated at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the number of ways of choosing 4 items from a set of 6. Find the force in newtons required for one pallet and convert it to kilonewtons. Multiply by the 8 pallets to get one ram's demand, then subtract 8 kN for the assistance provided by the ram's return spring. The foreman's figure is that per-ram result multiplied by the 9 rams. What is it in kN?

The result the flight-test engineer wants is the energy, in kilojoules, for 3 identical catapult launches after all corrections have been applied. A single launch propels a 52000 g drone to a speed in metres per second equal to the rate of change of the curve 3x^3 - 2x^2 with respect to x at x = 3. Find the drone's kinetic energy in joules, subtract 2 J for the energy lost in the release hook, and convert the result to kilojoules. Then subtract a further 29 kJ that the catapult's flywheel retains after each launch. The engineer multiplies this corrected per-launch figure by 3 for the 3 launches. What is the total in kJ?

The figure the safety auditor records is the total energy, in kilojoules, absorbed by a crash barrier over 8 test sessions of 4 impacts each, plus a 17 kJ allowance for the barrier's own spring-back. In each impact a 36 kg trolley, launched from a ramp 5 m long, strikes the barrier at a speed in metres per second equal to the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 12x + 32 = 0. Find the trolley's kinetic energy in joules and convert it to kilojoules; multiply by 4 for one session and then by 8 for all sessions, and finally add the 17 kJ allowance. What is the recorded total in kJ?

A regenerative-braking rig on a workshop bench captures the motion of a 55 kg flywheel cart, which runs on a track 12 m long. The cart moves at a speed in metres per second equal to the smaller of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 13x + 40 = 0. Find the cart's kinetic energy in joules and express it in kilojoules; this is the energy recovered into the battery in one cycle. During the same cycle a charger adds 24 kJ to the battery and the motor draws 27 kJ from it. The rig runs 11 identical cycles. What is the net change in the battery's stored energy over the 11 cycles, in kJ (negative if a loss)?

A luggage-handling system on an airport concourse 60 m wide moves 18 kg suitcases along a belt. The belt speed in metres per second is 8 times the greatest common divisor of 298 and 115. Find the kinetic energy in joules of one suitcase at that speed. There are 5 suitcases on the belt at any moment, so multiply by 5, and then add 17 J for the energy stored in the belt's tensioning spring. The system has 5 identical belts, so multiply the result by 5. What is the total energy in J?

The engineer is after the adjusted holding figure, in kilonewtons, for a clamp on a test block, and the clamp's rating is obtained only after two corrections. The block has a mass of 12000 g and accelerates at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 9x + 8 = 0. Find the force in newtons that gives the block that acceleration and convert it to kilonewtons. To that figure a 16 kN preload is added, and then a 17 kN hydraulic relief is subtracted. What is the adjusted figure in kN (negative if the relief exceeds the load)?

A 9000 g robotic lawn mower on a test rig moves at a speed in metres per second equal to 4 times the greatest common divisor of 386 and 284. Find the mower's kinetic energy in joules at that speed and express it in kilojoules. The rig's data logger adds 11 kJ for the energy stored in the blade flywheel, and then adds a further 13 kJ for the charge remaining in the battery, to give the mower's total on-board energy figure. What is that total in kJ?

The number the packaging line supervisor wants is the adjusted energy total, in joules, for 4 trays of 6 identical bottles each, after the rig's corrections. Each bottle has a mass of 4 kg and travels at a speed in metres per second equal to the larger of the two values of x that satisfy x^2 - 11x + 24 = 0. Find the kinetic energy of one bottle in joules, multiply by 6 for a tray, then by 4 for all the trays. The rig's controller then adds 4 J for the energy held in the conveyor's belt tension and subtracts 15 J for the energy lost to bearing friction. What is the adjusted total in J?

What the site engineer wants to know is how far the demand on a winch exceeds its 7 kN rating, in kilonewtons, with a negative answer meaning the winch is within its rating. The winch drags 5 identical crates, each of mass 85 kg, along a level ramp. Each crate accelerates at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the rate of change of 1x^3 - 4x^2 with respect to x at x = 4. Find the pull needed on one crate in newtons, multiply by 5 for all the crates, and convert the total to kilonewtons. Then subtract the 7 kN rating. What is the result in kN?

A container terminal uses straddle carriers to shift 195 kg test blocks along a 120 m apron. Each block is accelerated at a rate in metres per second squared equal to the larger of the two values of x for which x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0. Find the force in newtons needed to accelerate one block. Each carrier handles 4 blocks at once, there are 10 carriers in the fleet, and the terminal runs 4 identical shifts per day. Multiply the single-block force by 4, then by 10, then by 4 to get the day's combined force figure. What is it in N?

The figure the pump-station engineer needs is the usable energy, in kilojoules, of a 10 slug water-hammer test after a 14 kJ deduction. Each slug of water has a mass of 54000 g and moves at a speed in metres per second equal to 3 times the greatest common divisor of 92 and 396. Find the kinetic energy of a single slug in joules, multiply by 10 for all the slugs, and convert the total to kilojoules. Then subtract the 14 kJ absorbed by the surge tank. What is the usable energy in kJ?

A tow tractor of mass 180000 g operates on an airport apron at an air temperature of 22 degrees Celsius. Its acceleration in metres per second squared equals the area under the curve 1x^2 + 7x between x = 0 and x = 2. Find the force in newtons required to accelerate the tractor, multiply by 8 for the 8 tractors in the fleet, and convert to kilonewtons. The fleet runs 5 identical pushes per hour, so multiply by 5. Finally subtract 28 kN of assistance supplied by the apron's winch system. What is the resulting force in kN?
